messages:
Priya: heads-up — AtlasHealth POC hitting intermittent 429s during a bulk embeddings import tonight. They reported failures ~11:03pm PST and again at 11:22pm. Also flagged an unexpected usage charge on their trial invoice. Can we triage?
Alex: got it. do we have tenant id + route + a sample request_id?
Priya: tenant=atlashealth, route=/v1/embeddings, model=text-embed-3-small. sample request_id=req_0a12b3c4. customer run was ~50k docs with concurrency=10. logs below:
```
2024-12-12T06:58:03Z [rate-limiter] tenant=atlashealth route=/v1/embeddings status=429 token_bucket=0.12 burst_remaining=0
2024-12-12T07:03:12Z [ingest] req=req_0a12b3c4 client=atlas-importer conn=ws tokens=2400
2024-12-12T07:03:12Z [billing] tenant=atlashealth tokens_charged=2420
```
Priya: they also attached a screenshot of invoice line: "usage spike 2024-12-12 $42.10"
Alex: that token_bucket=0.12 looks suspicious — maybe fractional bucket leftover from streaming accounting. our default per-route cap for embeddings is 100rps with small burst windows.
Jin: I'll pull the rate-limiter traces now. @Priya can you confirm whether they used streaming websocket or normal POSTs?
Priya: they used websocket uploader to parallelize — 10 concurrent streams. they said each stream batches ~200 docs.
Leah: customer asks for a short-term quota bump for a demo tomorrow morning. can we do +2x for 24h? they may convert if demo completes.
BillingBot: Invoice lookup: tenant atlashealth shows usage spike on 2024-12-12, charge $42.10 (ticket BILL-1823 created). Manual credit requires finance approval.
Jin: quick note from traces: we see double-counting in token accounting on v1.4.0 when websocket streaming + batching are used. runtime v1.4.2 contains a fix. atlashealth is on hosted but pinned to older runtime variant.
Alex: mitigation options: 1) temporary per-route cap increase for atlashealth (500rps) for 24h; 2) route them to text-embed-3-medium which has higher soft caps; 3) apply temporary invoice credit while we root-cause.
Priya: option 1 + 3 seems best for sales. can you do the cap change, Jin? I'll ask finance for fast credit.
Jin: on it. increasing per-route cap for tenant=atlashealth route=/v1/embeddings to 500rps, expiry=24h. making change now.
ConsoleBot: change-applied: route-cap-update tenant=atlashealth route=/v1/embeddings old=100 new=500 expiry=2024-12-13T07:00:00Z by=jin.oncall
Jin: monitoring — 10m after change 429 count dropped from ~120/min to 0. will keep watching.
Priya: customer confirmed demo ran OK and no more 429s. they still want the invoice clarified.
Leah: good — please open a finance credit request for the $42.10 and note root-cause (streaming accounting bug on older runtime). I'll follow up with the AE.
BillingBot: credit-request opened: BILL-1823-CR. awaiting finance approval.
Alex: follow-up engineering action: prepare a runtime rollout note and backport the accounting fix to any pinned hosted variants. I'll create ENG ticket.
Priya: thanks all — marking this resolved for POC. tagging notes for handoff: // customer wants permanent higher cap if they go paid, and wants confirmation fix is rolled into their runtime variant.
Leah: copying AE to confirm next steps and pricing ask. :thumbsup:
thread_summary: AtlasHealth POC saw 429s during bulk embeddings via websocket; triaged to streaming token-accounting bug on older runtime. Temporary per-route cap increased and credit request opened for unexpected invoice charge.
